metadata.hardware_requirements: computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores).

nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Traffic volume data from a freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao in Shandong, China. Used for calibrating driving behavior parameters in the SUMO simulator and evaluating ramp metering methods.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: The paper explicitly states in the Data Availability section that data is available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations from raw images are extracted to reconstruct visual representations in the DRL method
nodes_process.description: Extract vehicle coordinates (xi, yi) from traffic camera frames to form binary position matrices mt for a control area of size X x Y.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, tools unnamed, area dimensions defined only in variables.

nodes_process.source_quote: we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state st
nodes_process.description: Combine N consecutive position matrices after zooming and down-sampling to a state matrix st of size (N, Xd, Yd).
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 0 tools named, all state dimensions specified in Table 1.

nodes_process.source_quote: A multitask learning strategy is implemented in the training process to improve learning efficiency.
nodes_process.description: Train a revised CNN (3 CNN layers, 2 FC layers) using the Adam optimizer, experience replay, and a target network to learn the Q-value, mean speed, and queue length simultaneously.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, standard libraries used, nearly all hyperparameters specified in Table 1.

nodes_process.source_quote: the proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator
nodes_process.description: Simulate the traffic scenario in SUMO from 7:50 to 9:00 a.m. comparing DRL, PI-ALINEA, and no-control baselines.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, tool named, core scenario parameters stated but specific SUMO version missing.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: Systematically remove information from one of eight control subareas and evaluate impact on travel time stability.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, procedure described but precise data removal mechanism (pixel-masking or coordinate-removal) is inferred.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 8: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time.
nodes_sink.description: Training progress metrics showing the reward stabilization and travel time reduction across one million training frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Model hyperparameters provided, but traffic demand and code require manual reconstruction; data available only upon request.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9: Vehicle travel times in the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Box-and-whisker temporal profiles of vehicle travel times across three control scenarios (No control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL).
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Outcomes are plausible based on DQN logic, but specific simulation config files for SUMO are not provided.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2: Mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Tabular presentation of average travel times per individual simulation run, documenting performance variance and gains.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Reports raw numbers for multiple runs, making comparative results verifiable if simulation setup is reproduced.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10: Temporal-spatial distribution of speed in (a) no-control; (b) PI-ALINEA; (c) DRL.
nodes_sink.description: Spatio-temporal heatmaps showing mean speed evolution along the mainline corridor under different controllers.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Directly aggregates microscopic simulator data; requires specific lane-wise sensor config inferred from paper text.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11: Queue length at the on-ramp.
nodes_sink.description: Temporal quantile plot comparing ramp queue buildup for the three methods during peak period.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Consistent with stated DQN rewards balancing queue and mainline speed, dependent on proprietary scenario data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12: Relationship of queue length and red ratio for (a) PI-ALINEA and (b) DRL.
nodes_sink.description: Correlation plot between signal red-time proportion and ramp queue length, with linear regression overlays.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Standard analysis of recorded control actions vs environmental response variables.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13: Queue length and occupancy for (a) PI-ALINEA and (b) DRL.
nodes_sink.description: Comparison of ramp queue dynamics relative to mainline occupancy peaks for standard vs proposed methods.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Correlates two internal simulator outputs; sensitivity dependent on provided DRL control logic.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 14: Downstream volume in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots tracking traffic volume at the merge point downstream, evaluating the ability to prevent capacity drop.
nodes_sink.size_estimate: Series of box plots over 70 mins
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Measures through-flow, an standard SUMO metric; input traffic volumes summarized in text diagrams only.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16: Travel time with perturbed input data.
nodes_sink.description: Perturbation analysis showing robustness of the visual controller when data from specific network subareas are excluded.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Qualitatively defined subarea masks make exact pixel-level perturbation matching difficult without source images.
